correctness.rationale: For every continuous test \(\phi(x)\), stationarity of an antiderivative gives \(\mathbb E[\phi(x)(By-C(x+p))]=0\), hence \(\mathbb E[y\mid x]=(C/B)(x+p)\). The residual is exactly \(\dot x/B\), so conditional-expectation orthogonality yields \(\operatorname{Var}(y)-(C/B)^2\operatorname{Var}(x)=B^{-2}\mathbb E[\dot x^2]\). Zero defect makes \(x\) constant on every support trajectory, then forces \(y\) constant and reduces bounded complete trajectories to equilibria. The quadratic generator identity independently reproduces the prior-implied temperature circle, and stationarity of \((x+p)^2/2\) removes the cross term needed for the three-term budget. All algebraic identities were replayed from the packaged checker.

value.rationale: The Vallis variables have direct physical interpretation as wind-driven current and east–west/mean temperature combinations, and rigorous work proves nontrivial compact chaotic recurrence for standard symmetric and asymmetric parameter sets. The accepted result identifies a stationary quantity not supplied by the prior localization geometry: the exact loss of current–temperature regression coherence is the mean-square current speed. It gives an equality-rigid diagnostic separating equilibrium mixtures from every genuinely time-dependent stationary state and inserts that kinetic defect into an exact universal quadratic budget. This provides a parameter-explicit consistency check for simulations or stationary data and a structural bridge between geometric localization and temporal variability, rather than a recomputation of a known equilibrium or Lyapunov exponent.
